newsitem.title: UK: Appleyard to take charges of 8.6 mln stg.
newsitem.headline: Appleyard to take charges of 8.6 mln stg.

text.p: British automobile distributor Appleyard Group Plc said on Monday that it was restructuring its dealership network which would result in exceptional charges of around 8.6 million stg in its 1996 results.
Appleyard said it was forced to restructure after major car makers had made changes in the size of territories and facilities that they required of distributors for their networks.
The distributor said it was closing 10 dealerships and selling two more, realising cash of 1.4 million stg.
Appleyard was planning to sell at least four more dealerships this year and would not invest additional capital at eight locations due to the absence of acceptable returns, it said.
The actual and planned disposals are expected to generate around eight million stg during 1997, including release of working capital.

Appleyard said, however, t was committed to investing in the separation of the Audi and Volkswagen brands at its Wishaw, Glasgow, Liverpool, Manchester, Durham, Sutton Coldfield, Henley and Reading sites.
"When these changes are complete, this division would operate 23 franchises from 37 sites," it said.

"The overall effect of these moves will be to reduce the overhead base of the passenger car division, to improve profitability by focusing on the core sites and to make it operationally positive," Appleyard said.
